newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Centre Democrats to quit government.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Centre Democrats to quit government.

text.p: Denmark's Centre Democrats said on Friday that they would leave the minority coalition government "as soon as is convenient".
A statement by the party said that it would continue to support the beleaguered government from outside the coalition.

The party, which has often described itself as a bulwark against the far left, said it was leaving the centre-left government because of its increasing dependence on the leftist fringe for its political survival.
The coalition on Thursday won parliamentary approval for its 1997 budget ater forging a deal with the far left Socialist People's Party (SPP) and Unity List parties.
Without the Centre Democrats, the Social Democrat-Radical Liberal rump coalition commands 71 seats in parliament compared to the combined rightist opposition's 83.
The SPP and Unity List hold the balance of power, with 13 and six seats respectively.
